title: Security & Region Pinning Review — Goldcrest Biometrics
summary: Review of region pinning, subprocessor list, KMS options (BYOK vs Redwood-managed), audit log retention, RBAC/SSO integration, and pilot scope for EU biometric workloads. Customer requires explicit EU residency for biometric PII and wants an approved subprocessor map. Discussed Dedicated vs Private deployments, fallback routing, and timeline for security review.
topics: audit logs, retention and SIEM integration
action_items: Maya Patel: Share subprocessor inventory CSV + attestation timelines (due 2026-08-10)
Ethan Chen: Run a synthetic latency benchmark from EU region against Dedicated config and share results (due 2026-08-14)

Marcus Li: Provide network diagram for onboarding Private VPC options (due 2026-08-13)

transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-08-05 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Noah (Redwood SE), Dr Ana Ruiz (CISO, Goldcrest), Marcus Li (Head Infra), Priya Nair (Legal), Owen Brooks (Platform)

Summary: Quick review of region pinning for biometric PII, expecting EU-only processing, BYOK discussion, subprocessors, and timeline for pilot.

Topics: data residency, subprocessor attestations, KMS, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, deployment options.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:08] Dr Ana: Ana here, hi.
[00:10] Marcus: Marcus here.
[00:12] Priya: Priya, legal.
[00:15] Owen: Owen, platform.
[00:18] Maya: Great, I'll hand to Ethan to kick off the technical summary, and then we'll go into the subprocessor and KMS questions.
[00:25] Ethan: Cool thanks. So Redwood provides multiple deployment modes, hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private VPCs. For your case with biometric data you said you need EU-only processing and no cross-border copies, correct?
[00:38] Dr Ana: Correct. EU residency only for raw biometric PII, we can tolerate derived embeddings being in the US after aggregation maybe, but raw inputs must stay in EU. There are PCI-ish export concerns for some customers too.
[00:52] Ethan: Understood. We can enforce region pinning at the routing layer so requests from your EU tenant are pinned to eu-west-1 capacity. We also have a Private deployment with a customer-managed control plane option if you require air-gapped or on-prem. The caveat is subprocessor chain — our hosted control plane currently uses some cloud services, we'll share an updated subprocessor inventory.
[01:12] Dr Ana: Can you confirm which subprocessors touch raw data? we've seen other vendors blur those lines.
[01:20] Ethan: Yes, good question. Raw tokens and KV cache for in-flight inference live on the inference node; Redwood-managed hosted service uses short lived ephemeral storage on GPU nodes. Subprocessors like metrics and analytics vendors get telemetry only, but some orchestration components run in region X. We'll send you the CSV that maps subprocessors by function and region.
[01:45] Marcus: For us it's about control and auditable attestations. We need proof that eu-hosted instances never replicate data outside region, and that KMS rotates keys under our policy.
[01:54] Maya: Right. We have two KMS flows: Redwood-managed KMS and BYOK via customer KMS/HSM. For BYOK we support a key-wrapping pattern where encryption keys are in your KMS (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault / external HSM), and Redwood holds wrapped keys. We also offer HSM escrow for long-term retention if required.
[02:20] Priya: Is there an option for split-key escrow across regions? we want to avoid single point of key compromise.
[02:27] Ethan: We do support split-key / envelope encryption with multi-region key stores — you can configure the key to live in eu only and use key policy that denies decrypt from other regions. Our docs have an example but we'll provide a diagram.
[02:41] Owen: Practically speaking, how do you prevent fallback to a US model when EU Dedicated pool is saturated? we've seen failover policies route to cheaper US endpoints.
[02:51] Noah: Good call. Routing policies are policy-driven — you can set strict region pinning, or set soft affinity with fallback. For strict compliance you'd set hard pinning which denies cross-region fallback. The tradeoff is availability during outages. We can configure automatic fallback disabled for your tenant.
[03:12] Dr Ana: Does hard pinning increase cost or latency?
[03:16] Ethan: Not necessarily cost, but availability tradeoffs. It could increase latency if we need to route to smaller dedicated pools; batching behavior might change slightly. We'll run benchmarks.
[03:30] Marcus: About audit logs — retention and SIEM exports. We need immutability and tamper-evidence plus integration with our Splunk stack.
[03:40] Maya: We provide audit logs for request metadata, model version, and routing decisions. Logs can be pushed to your SIEM via S3 export in the eu region or delivered over TLS to your log collector. Retention can be configured per contract. We'll share sample log schema.
[03:56] Priya: And is PII scrubbed from logs by default? we can't have raw biometric vectors in traces.
[04:03] Ethan: By default we redact full-text inputs in hosted logs — we capture hashes/ids for traceability. For Private deployments you control retention and redaction. We'll document the default redaction rules and provide an opt-in for additional scrubbing.
[04:20] Dr Ana: SOC2 / ISO evidence — can you provide the current certs and the last audit report under NDA?
[04:28] Maya: Yes, we can. We'll share SOC2 Type II report excerpts and ISO-27001 cert after NDAs. We also have pen testing summaries.
[04:38] Marcus: Subprocessor attestations — we need signed commitments that subprocessors storing eu data will abide by eu residency. Some vendors claim 'we can provide region' but storage still replicates metadata.
[04:50] Ethan: The subprocessor CSV will include region columns and whether subprocessors store data or only metadata. We can mark which subprocessors have EU-only tenancy.
[05:02] Owen: On RBAC — we want least-privilege roles. Can we map to our existing SAML groups?
[05:08] Noah: Yes. We support SAML SSO + SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is role-based with pre-built roles (admin, dev, auditor) and you can create custom roles. SCIM sync can map groups to roles and you can gate access to model ops.
[05:24] Marcus: Any caveats with offline backups or KV cache replication? our KV cache contains ephemeral state but could be sensitive.
[05:32] Ethan: KV cache is ephemeral and lives on node-local storage by default. For Dedicated you can configure no persistent checkpointing. For Private you can pick node storage encryption tied to your KMS. We'll show the cache lifecycle diagram.
[05:50] Dr Ana: About BYOK, does Redwood ever see the plaintext key?
[05:54] Ethan: No, never. We only get wrapped keys. Decryption happens in HSM boundary if you choose an HSM-backed key.
[06:02] Priya: Do you offer key escrow for regulatory e-discovery?
[06:06] Maya: We do provide an escrow option with strict controls and audit logs; it requires legal agreements. We'll put the process in the DPA appendix.
[06:18] Owen: For the pilot we want a Dedicated pool in eu-west-1 for 2 weeks with sample anonymized payloads. We'll measure latency at 95th percentile under 200ms.
[06:29] Maya: That sounds reasonable. We'll provision a Dedicated pool and run the benchmarks Ethan will run.
[06:35] Dr Ana: On subprocessors, can you commit to a standing notification for any new subprocessor that may touch data? we need 30 days notice.
[06:43] Maya: Standard is 30 days for material changes and we can include a clause in the contract.
[06:49] Marcus: Regarding regional backups and DR, do snapshots ever cross regions?
[06:55] Ethan: By default snapshots are region-contained but some analytics exports live in a separate region — we'll flag those in the subprocessor list. For hard pinning we'll ensure backups remain in eu.
[07:08] Priya: For the SIEM exports, is TLS mutual auth supported?
[07:12] Noah: Yes mTLS supported for log delivery endpoints.
[07:16] Dr Ana: What about model weights — are they ever moved to the US for optimization or kernel compilation?
[07:23] Ethan: Model compilation can happen in our build cluster. For open models we can compile in eu if required; for some proprietary accelerations we use prebuilt kernels. We'll note compilation locality in the model onboarding doc.
[07:40] Marcus: One more on subprocessors: if a subprocessor goes bankrupt or gets acquired, what's your process for re-assessing compliance?
[07:49] Maya: We run annual reviews, but for material events we trigger a re-evaluation and notify customers as per contract. We'll include the escalation path.
[07:59] Owen: Curious about billing: would Dedicated EU-only pool be priced differently?
[08:04] Maya: Pricing is based on reserved capacity; Dedicated in eu regions reflect local capacity rates. We'll send a pilot pricing estimate.
[08:12] Dr Ana: Ok. I think next step for us is to review the subprocessor CSV and the SOC2 excerpts, then confirm pilot scope.
[08:19] Maya: We'll send those today. Ethan will run the benchmarks and Noah will attach the log schema.
[08:26] Priya: We'll also send any regulatory language we need in the DPA.
[08:30] Maya: Great. Any final quick notes?
[08:33] Marcus: Please include sample log entries showing redacted inputs versus hashed ids.
[08:38] Ethan: Will do.
[08:41] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and action items.

End of recording.
notes: Customer emphasized biometric PII residency and wants hard pinning + BYOK in EU. Legal asked for DPA language and 30-day subprocessor notice. Practical pilot agreed: 2-week Dedicated eu-west-1 pool, benchmarks and log exports to Splunk via mTLS.
